See reference/files/marketstall.toml. marketplace snippet, package feed Marketplace The aggregated catalog of haybales visible in the Library Manager's AVAILABLE section; built by merging the project's local [[heaps]] with all remote subscriptions ([[markets]] + [[stalls]]) resolved into [[caches]] by refresh. Multiple remote feeds are supported. package list, library catalog haybale-marketplace The optional haybale package (barn/haybale-marketplace/) that owns the Library Manager UI — the library browser/overview/component editors, MarketplaceState, and the LibraryManager install/uninstall service. Carved out of haybale-studio per ADR-0001; the studio runs without it. The directory ~/.haywire/db/haybale_marketplace/ holds the user's global marketplace file. See haybale/marketplace. Library Manager (the plugin); marketplace dir (the ~/.haywire/db/ path) README.md Fully generated landing page for a haybale package. Lives at the package root (not shipped in wheel). Content: NOTES.md verbatim (if present) followed by the human component catalog (identical content to OVERVIEW.md), plus any <!-- marketstall:share-url --> marker blocks preserved verbatim. Rendered by PyPI (info.description) and git platforms — the universal pre-install discovery document reachable via every distribution method. Generated by haywire docs in the same pass as OVERVIEW.md/QUICKREF.md. The marker blocks are managed by haywire share (spec §6.6); the generator preserves them. — OVERVIEW.md Fully generated human-facing component catalog for a haybale package: components identified by label, grouped by category, one intent sentence each — no registry_keys. Lives inside the Python module directory (ships in wheel). Read from disk post-install by the Library Manager via lib.identity.folder_path. The marketstall's notes field names a supplementary page alongside it. Contrast QUICKREF.md, the agent-facing sibling keyed by registry_key. — QUICKREF.md Fully generated agent-facing component index for a haybale package: one line per component keyed by registry_key (the handle other Farmhand tools take), grouped by kind, with search_tags/deprecation flags. Hidden components are excluded. The tier-1 steering document a drilling agent fetches before requesting one component's deep doc from docs/. Lives inside the Python module directory (ships in wheel). Contrast OVERVIEW.md, the human-facing sibling keyed by label. — NOTES.md Hand-authored supplement inside the Python module directory (ships in wheel). Design rationale, known quirks, interaction patterns, example graph descriptions. Never touched by haywire docs. Prepended verbatim to the generated README.md; appended as "Additional Notes" in OVERVIEW.md. LIBRARY.md (old name, deprecated) haywire docs The deterministic CLI subcommand (uv run haywire docs <path>, or --all for every in-repo library in one load) that generates README.md, OVERVIEW.md, QUICKREF.md, and one deep doc per component under docs/<registry_key-with-dots>.md — for all 11 component kinds, not just nodes. Pure extraction: identity fields, NodeInstanceInspector introspection of a freshly-built instance for node ports/settings, and verbatim author docstrings — never an agent, never inferred prose. Ends with a coverage report flagging components with no description/docstring. Regeneration reconciles docs/, removing deep docs for components that no longer exist. Preserves <!-- marketstall:share-url --> marker blocks in the README verbatim (spec §6.6). Never modifies NOTES.md. Replaced the earlier agent-driven haybale-gen-docs skill, which was non-deterministic. haybale-gen-docs (retired skill, superseded) Compatibility Warning An advisory, author-declared notice that a graph saved by an older library version may not reflect a later behavioural change. Declared as an append-only history via BaseLibrary.compatibility_warnings(); each entry is a CompatibilityWarning(version, component, message). On load, the CompatibilityChecker fires it when a node's saved library.version is below the entry's version. Read-only — never mutates saved data; the suggested remedy is the Reset Node action. See ADR-0005. migration (implies data transformation — this never transforms), changelog CompatibilityChecker The stateless service run once inside Graph.load_from_dict that resolves which Compatibility Warnings fire for a loaded graph and writes NodeWarning records onto node state. Pure logic; takes a library-history lookup, returns findings. — NodeWarning An advisory record on NodeWrapperState.warnings (distinct from errors; does not affect is_valid()). First writer is the Compatibility Warning feature (kind="compatibility"). node error (errors invalidate; warnings advise) InstallType The mechanism axis of how a library reached this Python environment: REGULAR (site-packages), EDITABLE (pip -e, source stays on disk and hot-reloads), FOLDER (never pip-installed — discovered by scanning a folder path; today only builtin), or NOT_INSTALLED (not present in this environment at all — a catalog row the user could install; not "was removed", which leaves no LibraryInfo). Detected purely from a filesystem path, with no workspace context — LibraryDiscovery._detect_install_type() classifies REGULAR vs EDITABLE by whether the path sits inside site-packages; FOLDER libraries are discovered through a separate folder-scan path entirely. Distinct from Library Origin, the orthogonal "where did the code come from" axis. (new) install type (as a stand-in for provenance — mechanism and origin are different questions) Library Origin The origin axis of a library, orthogonal to InstallType: framework (this library IS the framework — currently only builtin, implied directly by InstallType.FOLDER), project_local (lives under this workspace's own barn/, per is_project_library()), pypi / git (came from a marketplace install with a catalog Haybale.source of that value), or unknown (an EDITABLE install with no catalog entry at all, e.g. a bare pip install -e ../some-other-repo outside the marketplace flow — origin is honestly unresolvable here, never guessed). Computed at the marketplace/studio layer (haybale_marketplace/library_origin.py), not in haywire-core, because only that layer knows the workspace root; LibraryRegistry/LibraryDiscovery stay workspace-agnostic and never compute it. origin.is_protected is True for framework and project_local — the single predicate the Library Browser's Required badge, the Uninstall-button gate, and the Disable button's block message all consult, replacing what used to be separately re-derived per call site. (new) origin (unqualified — always say Library Origin), source (collides with Haybale.source, the narrower catalog-only field this reads as one input) is_project_library() The low-level path-check primitive (is_relative_to(workspace_root / "barn")) that both Library Origin computation and unrelated dialog logic (read_os_from_pyproject's heap-vs-installed-wheel branching) depend on. Lives in haybale_marketplace/library_origin.py. Answers one narrow question — "is this under this workspace's barn/" — and is not itself the origin predicate; Library Origin calls it as one input alongside InstallType and Haybale.source. (new) project-local (as if it were the whole origin answer — it's one input to it) project_writable_libraries() Farmhand's write-target resolver (haybale_studio/farmhands/_helpers.py): every EDITABLE-mechanism install, regardless of whether its path sits under this workspace's barn/ at all. Deliberately broader than Library Origin's project_local — Farmhand's real need is "can I write this source," which any -e install satisfies, not "is this literally this workspace's own library." Renamed from project_local_libraries(), which implied the narrower, origin-axis meaning it never actually had. project_local_libraries (old name — collided in meaning with Library Origin's project_local, though the two diverge for a symlinked-in editable install of someone else's library) Distribution name The pip package name — haybale-studio, haybale-visiongraph, haywire-core. Authored as name in haybale.toml, which is canon; pyproject.toml's [project] name is a generated copy (PROJECT_FIELDS), and the installed distribution's metadata (ep.dist.name) is that copy observed at runtime. Read it as Haybale.name — never from the entry point, which is a copy of a copy and is absent entirely for InstallType.FOLDER libraries. What uv pip install/uninstall and every install_spec name. The haybale- prefix is a convention, not a rule: the framework-owned builtin library's distribution name is haywire-core, so a name must never be reconstructed as f"haybale-{stem}" — and a project scaffolded by haywire init gets hay-<base> instead. Also prefixes every component's registry key (haybale-example:node:Add, haywire-core:widget:NumberWidget): reg_key() is called with LibraryIdentity.name at all 10 call sites, so changing it orphans saved graphs. Not immutable, but changing it is a whole-project rewrite — the haywire rename CLI is the only supported path. (new) package name (ambiguous — could mean the Python module); LibraryInfo.distribution_name (removed field) Module name The importable top-level Python package — haybale_studio, haywire_core. Derived from the distribution name by module_of() (separators → _, lowercased), never authored separately; haybale-TEST_A → haybale_test_a. The canonical match key for linked_libraries and for hot-reload scope tracking (_get_tracking_scopes) — matching on the distribution name instead is a bug, since a hyphen yields a scope matching no module. (new) package name (ambiguous); distribution name (hyphenated — the un-normalized sibling) LibraryIdentity A library as loaded in this process: only what cannot be answered by a file read — id, folder_path, module_name, label (logged from inside the registry), linked_libraries (read during module registration), on_reload (read after eviction, when the files may be gone), file_watcher, plus version (needed at decoration time, before any render — the one field deliberately duplicated, per ADR-0025, and kept in step by bump_version.py and check_release_versions.py). Eight fields in code. Built once at import from haybale.toml; refreshed in place on file change by update_identity_from_toml(), which keeps the previous values rather than raising when the file is mid-write. Everything descriptive is read at the point of use as a Haybale instead, so an edit is visible without a reload — and rendering that falls back to the identity is a stale read with nothing to buy: a library whose file does not parse never loads at all, so an empty row only ever means the sub-render window between a write and the next read. library metadata (that's Haybale); do not add descriptive fields here — they go stale until the next reload; identity fallbacks in render code LibraryInfo A library as the Library Manager sees it: its declared metadata (a Haybale, read from disk or from the catalog) plus install state — row, identity, enabled, install_type. Built for installed libraries and for catalog rows that are not installed here, where the install-state fields carry their empty values and install_type is NOT_INSTALLED. The single type the Library Browser and Library Overview Editor consume, so "installed or available" is discriminated once at construction rather than re-derived by hasattr/isinstance/getattr at each render site. Carries no distribution-name field: that is row.name, canon per ADR-0025. Constructed only in haybale-marketplace's LibraryManager; the type itself lives in haywire-core. _LibView (the earlier filter-only precursor it replaces); LibraryInfo.distribution_name (removed — it echoed the generated [project] name and was empty for folder installs)

docs.title: Farmhand — the AI harness
docs.text:
Farmhand is Haywire's umbrella term for the AI harness that helps and supports a user with Haywire. It spans three surfaces of one concept, disambiguated by qualifier: the Farmhand server (in-studio MCP host), the farmhand tools (library-contributed capabilities), and the Farmhand plugin (the Claude Code side — proxy + onboarding skills). "Farmhand" unqualified means the whole harness.

Term Definition Aliases to avoid Farmhand The whole AI harness that helps/supports a user with Haywire — spanning the in-studio MCP server, the library-contributed tools, and the Claude Code plugin (proxy + skills). Qualify when a specific surface is meant (Farmhand server / plugin / proxy). MCP server alone (that's the server surface only), agent API Farmhand server The in-studio MCP server subsystem through which AI-agent clients operate the studio via library-contributed tools. The host (transport mounted at /mcp on the studio app, session registry, mcp SDK dependency) lives in haywire-studio; the SDK-free contribution seam (FarmhandRegistry, Farmhand/@farmhand, FarmhandContext) lives in haywire-core. The studio_* baseline tools ship in barn/haybale-studio, registering through the same folder-scan mechanism as every other library's tools. MCP server (ambiguous — any third-party MCP server) Farmhand plugin (farmhand4claude) The Claude-Code-only plugin distributed from github.com/going-haywire/farmhand4claude (npm @going-haywire/farmhand4claude): the Farmhand proxy (stdio↔HTTP MCP bridge) plus beginner onboarding skills. A graduating on-ramp (bootstrap → first graph → first library → first share), not a permanent power-user surface — that remains the haywire-live-studio skill. The "4claude" scopes the plugin, not the concept: skills are CC-specific, so the plugin is too; the proxy alone is portable to any MCP harness but is not the advertised path. Farmhand (unqualified, when the plugin specifically is meant) Farmhand proxy The stdio MCP server Claude Code spawns at session start that bridges to the Farmhand server's HTTP /mcp, forwarding tool/resource calls and re-emitting list_changed so studio tools appear mid-session with no reconnect. Reads the bearer token lazily from <ws>/.haywire/farmhand_token; runs in down-mode (a farmhand_studio_status sentinel) until the studio comes up. bridge, gateway (gateway is the SDK's word for the pattern, not this component) Studio identity sidecar (studio.json) The self-describing JSON the studio writes to <workspace>/.haywire/studio.json when it mounts the Farmhand endpoint: pid, port, project, project_path, started_at, host, role, url. Lets a later process (the farmhand4claude plugin's startup script) identify which project owns the studio on a port and decide to reuse / ask / clean up. Gitignored, machine-local; written only when farmhand.enabled. Sits beside farmhand_token. pid file (studioctl's is a bare integer; this is structured identity) farmhand A haywire MCP tool: one callable capability a Library contributes to the Farmhand server. A Component kind — a Farmhand subclass decorated @farmhand in the library's farmhands/ folder, registered via FarmhandRegistry, keyed {lib_id}:farmhand:{name}, surfaced to agents as {lib_id}_{name} (studio prefix belongs to haybale-studio's baseline). "MCP tool" remains the protocol-facing synonym (what tools/list returns). chore, command, contribution Error ledger A bounded, in-memory, sequence-numbered collection where every HaywireException registers at .log() time (registry-scan import errors wrapped in), queryable "since sequence N". First consumers are Farmhand's studio_get_errors and studio_verify_component. error log (file logs are unqueryable), exception history

docs.title: Marketstall distribution runtime
docs.text:
The runtime that backs the Library Browser's Refresh / Add Source / Edit File flow. Code: haywire.core.marketstall.

Term Definition Aliases to avoid Global marketplace The user-scoped ~/.haywire/db/haybale_marketplace/marketplace.toml. Holds the user's opt-in subscriptions ([[markets]], [[stalls]]) and optionally inline [[haybales]]. Per-machine, never project-scoped. user marketplace Project marketplace The project-scoped <project>/.haywire/marketplace.toml. Holds the project's own [[heaps]] (written by haywire init, including dev-repo libraries under --dev) and the [[caches]] populated by refresh. Never has [[markets]] or [[stalls]]. project file [[markets]] TOML section in the global marketplace declaring subscriptions to remote marketplace feeds. Each entry: url, ignores, doubles, blocked. Renamed from [[marketplaces]] (spec §14). [[marketplaces]] (legacy schema) [[stalls]] TOML section declaring subscriptions to remote marketstall feeds (single-author publish files). Each entry: url, ignores, doubles, blocked. Renamed from [[marketstalls]]. [[marketstalls]] (legacy schema) [[haybales]] TOML section listing one or more publishable library entries. Lives in marketstall.toml files; may also appear inline in marketplace.toml (PyPI-only / aggregator-publisher case). Replaces the older [[packages]] section name. [[packages]] (legacy schema) [[heaps]] TOML section in the project marketplace declaring path-based libraries (always installed editably). Written by haywire init; manually editable. Renamed from [[locals]]. [[locals]] (legacy schema) [[caches]] TOML section in the project marketplace holding the refresh result. Each entry is a fully-formed Haybale plus cache-only fields (via, last_seen, stale). Renamed from [[packages]] (project shape). [[packages]] (project shape; legacy schema) Subscription A [[markets]] or [[stalls]] entry in the global marketplace — the user's opt-in to follow a remote feed. Identified by URL. Idempotent: re-adding the same URL is a no-op. feed, source (overloaded) ignores Per-subscription array of names skipped from that source. Populated by the conflict-resolution prompt at Add Source time. Soft preference — the user picked another source. skip list blocked Per-subscription array of names the user actively rejected via the install-safety modal (§7.4). Stronger than ignores: blocked haybales are hidden from the Library Browser entirely and filtered out of the stale-rescue step so they never survive as stale=True. Un-blockable only by editing the marketplace file. denylist (don't use — it's not a denylist, it's per-subscription) doubles Per-subscription array of names that two [[markets]] entries silently dedup to. Diagnostic only. — Refresh The orchestrator (haywire.core.marketstall.refresh) that fetches every subscribed feed, resolves the candidate haybale list, applies blocked/ignores/heaps shadow/FCFS, and writes the result to the project [[caches]]. Triggered by Refresh button or auto-fires after Add Source. sync, update One-level-deep resolution The hard limit on remote-marketplace chains: a remote marketplace's own [[markets]] entries are ignored — only its [[stalls]] URLs and inline [[haybales]] are consumed. Prevents infinite recursion and bounds the refresh blast radius. recursive resolution Haybale (dataclass) The canonical dataclass for one entry available to install. Fields are documented in reference/files/marketstall.toml. Code: haywire.core.library.haybale. Renamed from MarketplaceEntry. MarketplaceEntry (legacy name) version (Haybale field) The version a marketstall entry advertises — the version its author published. NOT a floor: nothing resolves against it; its only job is the update comparison (installed < version ⇒ update available). Required; an entry without one raises MalformedMarketplaceError. Renamed from min_version, which was never a minimum. min_version (legacy name) Framework requirement The PEP 440 specifier naming the framework versions a library needs. Authored ONCE, in the haywire-core entry of the library's own pyproject — the only guard on the bare uv add path. The marketstall's require field is a projection of it, derived at write time so the two cannot disagree. Keep it as low as the library actually allows: a floor restricts consumers, not the author. requires_haywire (the old second carrier) Subscription (dataclass) The frozen dataclass for one [[markets]] or [[stalls]] entry: url, ignores, doubles, blocked. Renamed from RemoteSubscription; gained the blocked field. RemoteSubscription (legacy name) Conflict resolution The four-filter rule applied during refresh: blocked per subscription, then ignores per subscription, then heaps shadow (heaps always win), then first-come-first-served as the final safety net. Spec §8.2. — Stale Flag set on a project [[caches]] entry when a subsequent refresh did NOT re-resolve it. Renders as a red dot + "(stale)" suffix in the Library Browser. Stale + uninstalled entries are user-removable via the trash icon; stale + installed entries are locked until uninstalled. outdated, expired os field Per-haybale list of supported platforms. Declarable values: "macos", "windows", "linux". Source: each library's pyproject.toml [tool.haywire].os; copied into marketstalls by haywire share. Absent = "all platforms." "other" is the runtime sentinel for unmapped platform.system() results; never a declarable value. — RefreshOutcome Tri-state per-subscription refresh result: FRESH (HTTP 200, cache overwritten), CACHE_FALLBACK (HTTP failed, served from cache), UNAVAILABLE (HTTP failed, no cache). — RefreshReport Dataclass returned by refresh(): sources_fetched, sources_from_cache, sources_unavailable, unavailable_urls, haybales_resolved, new_stale, updates_available. The three sources_* counters partition the active subscription set. — MarketplaceState The AppState that owns marketplace orchestration. The UI calls state.refresh(), state.get_global(), state.get_project_haybales(), state.remove_stale_haybale() — never haywire.core.marketstall functions directly. — MalformedMarketplaceError Raised when a marketplace or marketstall file is invalid (TOML parse or schema violation). Library Manager surfaces this with an Edit File banner; the UI does not recover automatically. Renamed from MalformedGlobalMarketplaceError. — HTTP cache ~/.haywire/cache/<url-hash>.toml, one file per subscribed URL. Populated on successful fetch; consulted on fetch failure as a fallback. No TTL. Orphan cache files (no matching active subscription) are GC'd at end of each refresh. — Host provider One git host's URL conventions. Protocol with parse_blob_url / parse_raw_url / raw_url / blob_url methods. GitHub and GitLab ship in the first cut; Bitbucket and Gitea are deferred. Self-hosted instances declare themselves in ~/.haywire/config.toml. — Blob URL The browser-friendly URL to a file on a git host (e.g. https://github.com/alice/cool-libs/blob/main/marketstall.toml). Canonical persisted form for [[markets]] and [[stalls]] subscriptions. — Raw URL The fetch-friendly URL to a file's content (e.g. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alice/cool-libs/main/marketstall.toml). What the runtime actually HTTP-fetches. — Marketstall A TOML file hosted by a library author that lists their published haybale packages; consumed as a remote feed by haywire projects. Produced by haywire share. Lives at marketstall.toml in the repo root (single-author) or stalls/<dist-name>.toml (aggregator layout). marketplace snippet, package feed Marketplace The aggregated catalog of haybales visible in the Library Manager's AVAILABLE section. Built by merging the project's local [[heaps]] with all remote subscriptions ([[markets]] + [[stalls]]) resolved into [[caches]] by refresh. package list, library catalog Install-safety modal Three-button modal (Cancel / Block source / Install) interposing between every Install click and the actual uv pip install. Spec §7.4. Shows the haybale's origin as a clickable link; Block writes the haybale's name to the resolving subscription's blocked array. Fires on every Install — there's no first-time-only suppression. first-install modal (legacy term) Detect step The check_drift() step in SharePipeline (steps/detect.py), run early in every publish. Pure — it writes nothing, and has consumers beyond the Share flow. Reports five things per library: pyproject_missing (the only state that BREAKS a consumer's install, and the only one counted by has_drift), linked_missing (repaired automatically — see Linked registration), plus unused_declarations, pyproject_version_lag and unresolved as facts the author may act on or leave. The CLI declares undeclared imports for you and leaves the judgement calls alone; the Share flow offers each with a per-item choice. haywire deps check runs the same detect_share_drift() CI-side, read-only. Drift gate (retired — it gated on findings that are not defects) pyproject_version_lag Field on DepDrift carrying (dist_name, declared_floor, installed_version) tuples for declared haybale- deps whose ~=/>=/> floor is below the installed version. A fact, not a defect*: a floor states the OLDEST version that works, which requires resolving and testing candidates — static scanning cannot reach it, so "installed is newer" only means time passed. Never raised automatically, and excluded from has_drift. Scoped by entry point (haywire.libraries), which includes third-party haybales the publishing author does not control — another reason raising it would narrow consumer compatibility from the author's dev-machine state. version drift (implies a defect) updates_available RefreshReport field counting installed haybales whose cache version exceeds the installed distribution version. Drives the post-refresh toast count and the per-row ▲ indicator + "v0.X.X available" hint in the Library Browser. Informational only — nothing auto-updates. update count Aggregator layout The two-tier feed shape used by the official haywire marketplace (spec §11): a top-level marketplace.toml with one [[stalls]] entry per library, plus a stalls/ subdirectory with one marketstall file per library. Consumers can subscribe to the full feed (via the marketplace URL) or to a single library (via that stall's URL). Produced by scripts/generate_marketstall.py. per-haybale stall layout Bare-repo URL rejection Add Source refuses URLs that are just a repo (https://github.com/alice/cool-libs) with no file path — the resolver can't know whether to fetch marketstall.toml or a marketplace.toml from such a URL. The dialog asks for the blob/raw URL to the specific file. Spec §4.2. —

docs.title: Dependency manifests & drift (new)
docs.text:
A haybale library's dependencies live across three manifests with different audiences. They can drift; haywire provides tools to detect and reconcile.

Term Definition Aliases to avoid Project pyproject <project>/pyproject.toml. Audience: uv (workspace resolution). Lists what the project needs to run during dev. Never travels with a published library. root pyproject (acceptable, less precise) Library pyproject <library>/pyproject.toml, e.g. barn/haybale-foo/pyproject.toml. Audience: pip / PyPI / haywire share consumers. The [project] dependencies here is what travels with the published library and what pip resolves at install time. package pyproject linked_libraries Field in haybale.toml. Audience: haywire's runtime (LibraryManager). Lists which other haywire libraries must be enabled for this one to enable; gates Disable / Uninstall buttons via get_installed_dependents(). Each entry is a top-level Python package name (e.g. "haybale_core") — equal to the dependency library's LibraryIdentity.module_name top package. This is the canonical matching key: dependency resolution and hot-reload scope tracking (_get_tracking_scopes) both match a declared entry against each installed library's module_name (top-package-normalized), NOT its distribution name. Distribution name is empty for folder installs and is hyphenated — using it as the match key is a bug. Formerly a @library(dependencies=[...]) decorator kwarg; that kwarg now raises TypeError (see ADR-0025) — the field lives only in haybale.toml. @library(dependencies=[...]) (removed), library deps (ambiguous), runtime deps, distribution name (wrong key) Three manifest layers The conceptual triple — source imports / haybale.toml linked_libraries / library pyproject — that must agree for a library to ship cleanly. When they diverge (drift), haywire share may publish a package whose declared deps lie about what it needs. — detect_deps() Pure function in haywire.core.library.dep_detect. Statically AST-scans a library's source, resolves imports to distributions, and returns a DetectedDeps with one list shaped for haybale.toml's linked_libraries and another shaped for the library's pyproject. — DetectedDeps Frozen dataclass returned by detect_deps. Fields: library_linked (underscored module names of registered haywire libraries imported from source, destined for haybale.toml's linked_libraries), pyproject (distribution names + version specifiers — framework, registered libraries, and third-party), resolved (module → distribution map), unresolved (imports that couldn't be mapped). — HaywireLibrarySource Protocol with list_names() and get_library_distribution_name(id). The authoritative answer to "is this distribution a haywire library?" — by registration, not by name pattern. Live registry satisfies it; tests pass a fake. — EntryPointLibrarySource HaywireLibrarySource implementation backed by importlib.metadata.entry_points(group="haywire.libraries"). Used by CLI flows (haywire share) that don't bootstrap the haywire runtime. — DepDrift Dataclass from haywire.core.publishing.drift.model recording one library's dependency findings. Fields: lib_dir, pyproject_missing, linked_missing, unused_declarations, pyproject_version_lag, unresolved. has_drift is True iff pyproject_missing is non-empty — the rest are either reported facts or repaired automatically, and you cannot refuse to publish over something the tool always fixes. has_findings is True iff anything at all is set. Wrapped per-library into the pipeline's DriftReport (drifted / findings_only). — ShareError Base exception for every haywire share failure (haywire.core.publishing.pipeline.errors). Subclasses cover each pipeline step (PreconditionsError, ManifestError, VersionError, TagCollisionError, DocsGenerationError, MarketstallError, CommitError, PushError). Caught once at the CLI boundary in run_share_cli and per-step in the Share flow; never lets a raw traceback reach the user. DriftError (old, single-purpose exception; superseded — do not revive) ManifestError Raised when a library pyproject cannot be read or is invalid — unparsable TOML, unreadable file, or an undeclarable [tool.haywire].os value. One class for one condition, regardless of which step tripped over it: step 1 catches it to build a PreconditionFailure, the drift auto-fix lets it propagate. Named for the condition, not the step. DriftError, MarketstallError (both name a step, not the fault) PreconditionFailure One reason a project cannot be published, as reported by step 1. Carries message (what is wrong), remedy (what to do about it — computed from repo state where that helps, e.g. naming the branches that contain the current commit), and an optional fix_id naming a repair the pipeline can perform in place. Replaces the bare failure string, whose embedded newlines and indentation rendered correctly in a terminal and collapsed to one line in the UI. failure string, error message Remediable precondition A PreconditionFailure carrying a fix_id. Offered only when the repair needs no user input and is fully determined by repo state — plus one deliberate exception, setting origin, because a repo with no remote is the terminal state of haywire init and so the failure a first-time sharer hits by construction. auto-fix (implies it happens without asking) Diff modal The haywire.ui.modals.diff_modal Popup that previews proposed changes and offers up to two action buttons + Cancel. Generic — any "preview changes, choose how to apply" surface can reuse it. — Undeclared import A distribution the source imports that the library pyproject does not declare. The one dependency state that BREAKS a consumer's install, so it is the only one has_drift counts and the only one whose "leave it" answer is recorded (undeclared_acknowledged). Scoped to the pyproject only — a gap in linked_libraries is a Linked registration, not an import failure. missing dep (ambiguous — missing from which manifest?) Linked registration A registered haywire library the source imports that haybale.toml's linked_libraries does not list (linked_missing). Applied AUTOMATICALLY wherever it is detected — never offered as a choice, because there is nothing to decide: detect_deps emits a name here only when the source imports it AND it resolves to an installed registered library, so the entry is provably true, carries no version specifier, and narrows nothing for consumers. Reported rather than silent because it edits a hand-authored file. Applied identically on all three surfaces that touch it — haywire share CLI, the Share wizard's Review screen, and the Library Overview Editor's Refresh button — all reading DriftReport.linked_registrations. undeclared import (wrong — it is not an import failure), decorator registration (retired — the field left @library(...) in ADR-0025 and the code names it linked_missing) Unused declaration A declared dependency the source never imports. Inert for consumers, and indistinguishable from a dynamic import detect_deps cannot see, so removal is offered per item and never pre-selected. extra dep, obsolete dep Version floor lag A declared ~=/>=/> floor sitting below the version installed on the author's machine. A fact, not a defect — see pyproject_version_lag. The Share flow defaults every floor control to keep, so an untouched screen writes nothing. stale floor, outdated pin (both imply a defect) require The marketstall entry's framework requirement, as a full PEP 508 token identical in shape to the library's own pyproject entry: haywire-core>=0.0.38, or the bare haywire-core when the author deliberately declared no floor. Absent means undeclared — a state distinct from the bare name, which is why the field carries the package name rather than a bare specifier. Derived from the library's own floor at write time by haywire_core_requirement(), never authored beside it, so the two cannot drift. Read by check_require() as an advisory pre-install gate. requires_haywire (the old bare-specifier field; removed, no fallback) DiffSection One labelled block inside a diff modal: title + additions (green +) + removals (red −) + unchanged (dim) + optional note. —

docs.title: Settings System
docs.text:
See architecture/settings for the resolution chain and registry mechanics; see components/settings for authoring.

Term Definition Aliases to avoid NodeSettings Base class for node-local settings; subclassed as an inner class on a @node class; class name becomes the accessor (self.filter, self.output, etc.); never registered with the global registry Config, options, Bag, Settings (avoid bare Settings for node inner classes) GraphSettings The fourth Settings flavour (ADR 0022), parallel to NodeSettings: per-instance cells, never registered with the global registry, carries a _graph backref instead of _node (which stays None unconditionally — structurally disables promotion and the Setting-row menu's promote entries with no special case in those surfaces). One framework-provided bag today, GraphProperties, owned per-graph as graph.props and serialized under the graph's "props" key Graph props, graph bag FrameworkSettings Base class for framework/app-defined settings schemas; subclassed with namespace=; auto-registers via _pending_global at registry init; cls._registry is set by the registry so instances need no explicit injection — LibrarySettings Base class for library plugin-defined settings schemas; subclassed with namespace=; registered via BaseRegistry hot-reload machinery; same cls._registry auto-wiring as FrameworkSettings — setting() The descriptor that declares a typed, serializable field within any Settings subclass option, param, prop CHOICES Builtin IType(STRING) whose identity declares widget_key = SELECT_WIDGET but carries zero options — every declaration site supplies its own via widget_config={"options": [...] \| {value: label} \| callable}. Identity STRING↔CHOICES adapters (both directions, pure passthrough) let a plain string port connect to or promote from a CHOICES-typed one with no special case. Replaces the old choices= sugar. The callable shape is safe only on a setting() field (promoted or not) — see live widget_config callable below; a plain (non-promoted) port constructed with a callable there raises TypeError at construction time. See ADR 0017 choices (the removed setting(choices=...) parameter), enum type, *_SEL type widget key The registry key (a plain string, e.g. builtin:widget:SelectWidget) selecting which BaseWidget subclass renders a field or port. Stamped on a setting() descriptor's widget_key attribute exactly once — at __set_name__ for a class-body field, or at the end of __init__ for a registry-constructed one (registry.define(...), file auto-define) — never re-resolved at render time. An explicit widget= dict wins; otherwise it comes from the field's IType's declared identity (@type(widget_key=...)). See ADR 0017 resolved_widget_key (removed — no render-time resolution), widget hint transient widget config The {"key", "config"} dict returned by WidgetCls.config(...) (IWidget.config), passed as setting(widget=...) to pin an explicit widget class + properties for a field, overriding the IType's declared default. Distinct from widget_config=, which layers bare property overrides (e.g. {"options": [...]}) on top of whichever widget was already selected. Called "transient" because it is a plain dict computed at declaration time, not a persisted object — nothing about it is serialized itself; only the stamped widget_key/widget_config result is retained on the descriptor widget spec, widget hint dict live widget_config callable A callable placed in a port's or field's widget_config (e.g. {"options": lambda: ...}), resolved at widget render time (SelectWidget.build(): if callable(options): options = options()). Safe on a setting() field and on a promoted port — Settings.to_dict() never serializes widget_config, and a promoted port is not serialized at all (regenerated from settings on load, ADR 0019), so the callable never needs to survive a save/load cycle. Unsafe on a plain (non-promoted) port — the port has no descriptor to fall back on, so the callable IS the only copy; DataPort.__post_init__ raises TypeError at construction time (via is_cattrs_serializable) rather than letting it reach to_dict()/json.dumps later. See ADR 0018 (plain-port raise) and ADR 0019 (promoted ports never serialize) dynamic options callable mirrors A setting() parameter that links a node field to a FrameworkSettings or LibrarySettings field (or any field on a DIFFERENT class), inheriting its default with per-node override capability. Must not reference a field on the same bag — raises ValueError shadow, watch, reference shadow() Convenience factory: setting(mirrors=src, **kwargs). A writable mirror — per-node writes are allowed and stored as overrides; unset, it tracks the source's live value mirrors, watch watch() Convenience factory: setting(mirrors=src, ui_state=UiState.DISABLED, promotable=Promotable.OUTLET, **kwargs). Renders as a greyed, non-interactive widget and is outlet-only-promotable by declaration. Writes are not structurally blocked (no AttributeError) — read-only-ness is a naming convention, not an enforced guarantee shadow, mirrors, UiState graph mirror / graph() The graph-tier mirror factory (ADR 0022): graph(src=...) declares a node-bag field that mirrors a field on a GraphSettings bag, giving framework < graph < node resolution. Distinct from the registry-key mirrors/shadow()/watch() family — validates src eagerly (TypeError unless its owner is a GraphSettings subclass) and is wired cell-to-cell against the owning graph's bag (located via BaseGraph.settings_bag_for()), never through the registry notification channel. "Unset tracks, set ignores" per hop, composing transitively. A field on a bag with no reachable graph holds its plain descriptor default and is not live — no registry fallback, a deliberate scope decision (see the ADR's rejected alternatives) shadow (do not conflate — different channel), graph shadow UiState Per-field, per-instance presentation state of a setting in the properties panel: NORMAL | DISABLED (visible but non-interactive) | HIDDEN (row not rendered; a fully-hidden category hides its header). Pure chrome — a DISABLED or HIDDEN field stays fully readable/writable from code, keeps its value, and serializes normally; UiState itself is never persisted (recomputed from the descriptor seed ui_state= plus runtime set_ui_state calls). Imperative API set_ui_state(name, state) / set_ui_state_all(state, category=None) (category is a selector, never a state store) announces transitions on the dedicated UI-state channel (subscribe_ui_state, cb(name, UiState)); declarative same-bag gating via enabled_when (contributes at most DISABLED) and visible_when (contributes HIDDEN) metadata. bag.effective_ui_state(name) composes all sources by severity max (NORMAL < DISABLED < HIDDEN) — the one oracle consumed by panel rows and the Setting-row menu. Hiding never unpromotes: graph structure never depends on UiState (ADR 0020). (new) ui_disabled (removed boolean API), ui_visibility, visibility flag Promotion Assigning a direction to a value-bearing setting and surfacing it as a DATA port. A promoted port and its setting are one cell, two views — the port borrows the setting's DataField cell by reference and its id IS the setting's storage_key. Promotion state lives in the owning settings bag (Settings._promoted_keys, storage_key → direction) — the single source of truth. The promoted port is regenerated from settings on load, never serialized in the ports block (ADR 0019); promote_setting records the promotion and demote_setting clears it (mirror operations). Two verbs (promote(direction) / demote), three directions (inlet / outlet / config — see ADR 0014's reintroduction note). Which directions a field may ever be promoted to is gated by setting(promotable=Promotable.NONE\|INLET\|OUTLET\|CONFIG\|INPUT\|ALL) (default ALL), via the single eligible_promotion_directions() oracle shared by promote_setting (raises for an ineligible direction) and the Setting-row menu (hides ineligible entries). Direction- and link-aware editing surface (decision 7bA, revised 2026-07-07): a promoted field's label carries the → glyph (→• label when also locally-set). A setting promoted to an inlet replaces its widget with a literal "promoted" label — the graph owns the value; the row hint (tooltip + data-hint) reads "promoted to inlet" while unlinked or "driven by inlet" once an edge is connected. A setting promoted to an outlet keeps its editable widget (the setting is still the source of truth), hinted "promoted to outlet". The row carries data-promoted-direction="inlet"\|"outlet" and data-hint. Promote/Demote/Reset live in the Setting-row menu; the settings panel is the sole promote surface (the canvas node menu no longer offers promotion; the port right-click keeps "Detach from setting"). See ADR 0014 (direction model + one-cell-two-views) and ADR 0019 (settings-owned state + non-serialized regeneration, superseding 0014's amendment) Exposing, hoisting, wiring a setting promoted inlet / promoted outlet The two promotion directions. A promoted inlet lets an edge drive the setting (the panel widget is gone as soon as the promotion exists, linked or not); a promoted outlet lets the setting drive downstream consumers. A watch() field is outlet-only by declaration (promotable=Promotable.OUTLET, seeded by the watch() factory itself — no separate structural override). A promoted config field behaves like a promoted inlet in the Properties panel (widget replaced by a static "promoted" label, hinted "promoted to config") but has no pin at all — never linked, never driven by an edge; its live widget renders instead wherever a CONFIG port's widget already renders (Ports Panel / node card) — is_linked_lazy A DataPort flag set on every promoted outlet: it forces any linked edge to lazy (pull-on-demand) propagation so an out-of-frame setting write doesn't propagate eagerly. Paired with an on_changed → propagate subscription that triggers the deferred pull; the flag alone is inert — freeze-on-disconnect Demote (and any structural action) never resets a promoted setting's value: whatever the shared cell holds stays. Recovery to the default is an explicit reset() — accessor name The inner NodeSettings class name as it appears on the node instance (e.g. class filter → self.filter); must not collide with existing BaseNode attributes settings name, bag name SettingsRegistry The central registry that holds all global setting schemas and their TOML-sourced values; used for the full resolution chain; inherits BaseRegistry hot-reload machinery — Three-tier resolution The precedence chain for a settings value (highest-priority set tier wins): local instance value → workspace TOML set → global TOML set → descriptor default. Tiers are set-or-unset; there is no "override" strength — cache Transient, non-serialized per-node storage for computation buffers or memoization temp, scratch store Persistent, serialized per-node internal state not shown in the UI private state

docs.title: Graph Management
docs.text: Term Definition Aliases to avoid GraphEntry A runtime container for one open graph: holds the Graph, Editor, file path, unsaved flag, session set, and per-graph Interpreter. Concrete implementation of the GraphContainer protocol in haybale-haystack Graph slot, graph handle GraphContainer A protocol implemented by anything that can host a graph in GraphEditor: requires binding_id, editor, path, unsaved, display_name, and save(). GraphEntry is the haystack-flavoured implementation. See haybale-graph-editor Graph host, graph holder GraphAppState The app-wide registry mapping binding_id → GraphContainer. Source libraries (haystack, future cloud-graph libraries) register / unregister / rekey their containers here; GraphEditor reads from it on every render. Lives at app_data[GraphAppState] Graph registry, graph index Haystack A named, curated selection of GraphEntry's stored as a TOML file in haystacks/; records which graphs are open and which should auto-execute on load. See architecture/graph Session (overloaded with browser sessions), workspace (overloaded with layout), setlist, graphset HaystackEditor The left-slot editor that lists all open graphs, provides play/stop per row, and save/load haystack actions in the header GraphManagerEditor (renamed) GraphRunSettings A purely-local (never registry-backed) Settings bag owned by a GraphEntry that records how the entry runs within its Haystack — e.g. the autorestart flag. Persisted per-entry in the haystack TOML, not in the .haywire graph file. Distinct from the Execution Pipeline vocabulary (Assembly/VM/Flow), which is about running a graph, not policy for whether/how an entry runs Execution settings (collides with the VM/Assembly engine vocabulary), entry config

docs.title: UI / Workspace System
docs.text:
See architecture/studio for the studio as a product; components/editors, components/panels, components/themes, components/skins for authoring.

Term Definition Aliases to avoid Editor A full-slot UI component occupying one workspace Slot (ACTION, CONTEXT, EDIT, INFO); one instance per slot per session Panel (Panels are sub-components of editors), view Panel A context-sensitive sub-section rendered inside a panel-aware editor (e.g. Properties); appears/disappears based on poll(); always wrapped in .hw-panel container Tab, widget (too generic) Ports Panel The Panel under the ports Scope (PortFocus, available when a node is selected) that lists the selected node's inlets, outlets, and config ports. Renders each port's live Widget (the same one the node card shows, honouring should_show_widget()) where one applies, and a read-only id/type row otherwise — a second editing surface for ports whose Skin omits the Widget (e.g. flow-direction skins) port inspector, ports list PortFocus The Scope (id="ports", available when active_node is set) that hosts the Ports Panel — the selected node's full port list. Distinct from PinFocus (id="pin"), the per-pin right-click context-menu scope keyed on active_port ports scope PinFocus The Scope (id="pin", available when active_port is set) for the per-pin right-click context menu (hosts PortInfoPanel). Distinct from PortFocus (the node-scoped ports list). Was named PortFocus before the ports list took that name per-pin menu scope Scope A named tab within a panel-aware editor that groups panels (e.g. node, ports, graph, edge) Context (overloaded), category Hidden component A registered component (node, skin, theme, etc.) whose hidden=True field on its BaseIdentity excludes it from author-facing selection UIs (Add-Nodes menu, node search, skin/theme pickers). It stays fully registered, resolvable by registry key, and functional in existing graphs — hidden affects presentation as a choice, not existence. Browsing/debugging surfaces (marketplace, component editor) ignore hidden and still show it. hidden is the single canonical hide-from-selection mechanism. Primary use: framework-internal and testing components. Internal component, invisible component (avoid — it's not invisible everywhere), unlisted component Selection axis The set of currently-selected elements — EditState.selected_nodes / selected_edges (sets of ids). The command target: the elements a right-click menu, copy, paste, or delete acts upon. A lone right-clicked element is a selection of one. Distinct from the Active axis. selection state, current selection Active axis The single primary element of a selection — EditState.active_node / active_edge, at most one of which is non-None at a time (a node and an edge are never simultaneously active; setting one clears the other). The inspector subject: the element whose props / ports / settings / errors the Properties panels render, and the element that wears the distinct active highlight. Set by an explicit single-element focus gesture (plain-click or the active-promotion shift-click — see Active-promotion); cleared to None by any bulk or programmatic selection (drag-box, paste, deselecting the active element) — those produce a selection with no primary, so the single-element inspector panels hide while SelectionFocus still shows for batch ops. Distinct from the Selection axis. active node (overloaded with CONTROL node — see Node Behaviors), focused node; next(iter(selected_nodes)) (the old non-deterministic derivation — removed) SelectionFocus The Scope (id="selection", available when any node or edge is selected) that hosts the unified right-click command menu — Copy / Paste / Delete and the batch node ops (redraw / revalidate / reset), each acting on the whole Selection axis. The single command-menu pipeline for both lone and multi-element right-clicks. Distinct from NodeFocus / EdgeFocus, which remain for the single-element inspector (NodeFocus) and single-only verbs like edge reconnect (EdgeFocus). Also distinct from ToolbarFocus — SelectionFocus is the right-click surface; ToolbarFocus is the floating-toolbar surface; the floating toolbar's overflow (⋯) reaches back into SelectionFocus panels. selection scope, multi-select menu Floating toolbar A persistent, Miro-style command surface anchored above the Selection axis's on-screen bounding box whenever the selection is non-empty. A second command surface alongside the right-click menu, not a replacement. Rendered with NiceGUI panels (ToolbarFocus) into a persistent, no-backdrop Popup by SelectionToolbarProvider — the panel-render sibling of SessionContextMenuProvider. Python owns both content and the positioned container. The canvas (Vue) computes the selection's screen bounding box and emits a low-frequency selectionBounds event on selection-change and on pan/zoom/drag end, plus selectionBoundsHide on gesture start (Miro hide-during-gesture rule — no frame-rate traffic); the provider shows / setPositions / hides the Popup in response. Its curated face is Copy · Delete · ⋯, rendered horizontally as icon-only buttons (hui.icon_action) into a ui.row — deliberately unlike the right-click menu, which is a vertical column of labelled rows. The ⋯ overflow re-opens the SelectionFocus right-click menu (via ContextMenuSelectedEvent) so the batch ops live in one place. selection toolbar, action bar, hover toolbar; do not call it a "context menu" (that is the right-click surface) ToolbarFocus The Scope (id="toolbar") authors register floating-toolbar panels against — the curated face (Copy · Delete · ⋯). Distinct from SelectionFocus (the right-click surface). Copy/Delete panels declare focus=ToolbarFocus but actions=SelectionContextActions (reused); the ⋯ panel uses actions=ToolbarActions whose open_overflow_menu re-opens the SelectionFocus menu. Polled by SelectionToolbarProvider, not by the right-click provider. toolbar scope Replace-then-act The right-click selection gesture: right-clicking an element outside the current selection first replaces the selection with just that element, then opens the menu; right-clicking an element already in a multi-selection leaves the selection intact and acts on the whole set. The convention shared with Blender / Figma / n8n. right-click select Active-promotion The shift-click selection law (model B, Blender convention): shift-clicking an element always walks toward it until it is the active element, then drops it. Precisely — shift-click an unselected element → add it and make it active; shift-click a selected-but-not-active element → selection unchanged, promote it to active; shift-click the active element → deselect it (active → None). Removing an element from a multi-selection via shift-click is therefore a two-step gesture (promote, then drop). Plain (non-shift) click replaces the selection with the one element, which becomes active. Plain-click on empty canvas clears everything. There is no separate ctrl/alt deselect modifier. toggle-select (the pre-active behaviour — removed) Slot One of the four named positions in the AppShell where an editor is mounted, identified by a SlotName: ACTION (left edge), CONTEXT (right edge), EDIT (centre), INFO (bottom). Each slot = bar + area Area (deprecated), pane, region, zone; left/main/right/bottom (former slot names — removed) SlotName The StrEnum of the four slot identifiers: ACTION / CONTEXT / EDIT / INFO, with string values 'action' / 'context' / 'edit' / 'info'. A member is a str, so it serializes to its value in workspace_state.json and the hw-slot-<value> DOM ids with no conversion. SlotName(x).label gives the human-facing name (e.g. 'Edit') slot string, slot key Bar The control strip attached to a Slot; either a tab bar (horizontal, for EDIT/INFO) or an icon bar (vertical, for ACTION/CONTEXT) — default_slot The @editor() decorator parameter and EditorIdentity field that declares which Slot an editor occupies by default; a SlotName (ACTION / CONTEXT / EDIT / INFO), defaulting to SlotName.EDIT. The decorator coerces a bare string value and raises ValueError on an unknown one canvas_area (deprecated) slot snapshot The persisted state of one slot — a plain dict produced by Slot.to_snapshot() with keys active_key (the active binding id), visible, size, and editors (the per-tab list). Keyed by SlotName value in workspace_state.json. There are no per-slot state dataclasses — all four slots use this uniform dict shape SlotState / MainSlotState / BottomSlotState / TabState (former dataclasses — removed), active_tab_key (removed; the field is active_key) AppShell The top-level layout component composed of: TopBar + ActivityBar + ACTION/CONTEXT/EDIT/INFO Slots + ContextBar + StatusBar. See architecture/studio/app-shell Shell, frame TopBar The 48px bar along the top edge of the AppShell; contains the app name, workspace switcher, and global actions Header, navbar StatusBar The 24px bar along the bottom edge of the AppShell; shows session info and status messages Footer, info bar (Info Bar is a Panel pattern, not the StatusBar) ActivityBar The 48px icon bar on the left edge; switches editors in the ACTION Slot; styled with hw-slot-bar hw-slot-bar-icons Left sidebar, toolbar ContextBar The 48px icon bar on the right edge; switches editors in the CONTEXT Slot; styled with hw-slot-bar hw-slot-bar-icons Right sidebar MainTabBar The horizontal tab bar above the EDIT Slot; switches between tabbed edit editors; styled with hw-slot-bar hw-slot-bar-tabs Middle tabs, EditTabBar BottomTabBar The horizontal tab bar above the INFO Slot; switches between tabbed info editors; styled with hw-slot-bar hw-slot-bar-tabs Bottom tabs (use only for the metadata key) hw-slot-bar CSS base class for all slot bars (both icon bars and tab bars) hw-tabs (deprecated) hw-slot-bar-tabs CSS modifier for horizontal tabbed slot bars (MainTabBar, BottomTabBar) hw-tabs (deprecated) hw-slot-bar-icons CSS modifier for vertical icon slot bars (ActivityBar, ContextBar) — ScopeToolbar The vertical strip of 36×36px square buttons inside the PropertiesEditor that switches the active Scope Scope bar, scope selector Session A per-browser-connection state object; one per connected client. See architecture/session-and-state Connection, client SessionContext The state bag passed to every editor and panel render call; contains active graph, node, edge, and theme references Context (acceptable shorthand), state Workspace A named layout preset that records which editor occupies each slot; saved to .haywire/workspace_state.json. See architecture/studio/workspace Layout, perspective Skin A BaseSkin subclass that renders the visual shape of a node on the Graph Canvas; operates outside the .hw-panel cascade and uses only --hw-node-* and --hw-canvas-* tokens. See components/skins Renderer (Skin is canonical in code), style Widget An inline UI control bound to a port's value. Rendered inside the port's row on the node card (by the Skin), and — independently — inside the Ports Panel; the same port may have a live Widget instance in both surfaces at once, each with its own model subscription. See components/widgets Control, field input BaseWidget The single canonical widget base class (in haywire.ui.widget). Authors implement build() (construct the NiceGUI tree) and may either call the bind() sugar for flat-scalar fields or override the on_model_changed() floor hook for arbitrary model→view sync. Lives on the UI side of the agnostic line; reaches the model only through DataPort. See adr/0007 SimpleWidget (removed — folded into BaseWidget) ShowWidgetStrategy Per-port enum (NEVER, NOT_LINKED, WHEN_LINKED, ALWAYS) declaring whether a port's Widget is rendered for each link state. Resolved by DataPort.should_show_widget() against is_linked(). Direction defaults: inlet NOT_LINKED, outlet NEVER, config ALWAYS. See adr/0003 Widget visibility flag Theme A named set of CSS tokens (WorkbenchTheme) or per-node-type colour rules (NodeTheme); session-scoped for workbench. See components/themes Style, skin (Skin is distinct) Graph Canvas The Vue/NiceGUI hybrid component where nodes and edges are visually displayed and edited. See architecture/studio/canvas Canvas (acceptable shorthand), viewport Host slot The .ui-node-slot (ui.column, one per node, stable id) that the graph-editor wraps around a node's card. It owns the applied size: UINode._apply_size writes a manual axis as a minimum (min-width/min-height, never a hard size and never overflow — content that needs more room expands the node, so pins/widgets/edges never clip) here (never on the card), stamps data-size-adapt, and it is what the ResizeObserver measures and the resize gadget targets. Skins are size-agnostic; size and measurement live here. node slot, card wrapper size_adapt The per-node, per-axis mode ("auto" · "manual_width" · "manual_height" · "manual", default "auto") on NodeProperties deciding whether a card axis is measured-from-render (auto — the host-slot ResizeObserver writes the measured offset into props.width/height) or fixed-by-the-user (manual — set via the resize gadget). One props.width/height pair; size_adapt says which axis the observer owns vs. which the user fixed. size mode, resize mode Resize gadget The single-node, 8-handle JS transform box drawn in canvas.vue (content space, inside #node-container) around a lone-node selection. Fixes node size by dragging a grip — zero per-node DOM (one gadget total). A top/left drag pins the opposite edge (resize + move composition). On release it emits UserResizeEndEvent, committed by process_resize_end as one undoable fence (size + optional move). Replaces the old per-node _add_resize_handle (removed). resize handle (removed), size box hui The haywire.ui.elements wrapper module; encodes design-system rules into reusable Python functions; prefer hui.* over raw NiceGUI/Quasar calls for any pattern it covers haywire.ui.elements (use hui as the import alias) PanelLayout The container handle passed to BasePanel.draw(). A context manager bound to the panel's container — not a façade over hui. Panels render via with layout: then call hui.* directly; hui is the single rendering vocabulary. The only content helper it carries is expansion_section, which threads container-bound expansion-state persistence. See components/panels layout (the draw arg); not "layout helper" — it is not a façade CSS token A --hw-* CSS custom property that encodes a design-system value (colour, size, shadow); every structural colour in the app must reference a token, never a hardcoded value CSS variable (CSS token is the project term) Compact-fields A container-query–based responsive layout system for dense settings/property panels; activated by the compact-fields CSS class on the outer column Dense layout, settings layout Ghost pin The visual indicator (low-opacity colour via --hw-ghost-pin) on a port that is unconnected; rendered by node skins Unconnected pin, empty pin

docs.title: Modals (new)
docs.text:
haywire.ui.modals — the canonical set of reusable Popup-based modal dialogs. Use these instead of inline ui.dialog() for any new modal UI; the per-modal helpers carry the design-guide chrome (--hw-popup-shadow, --hw-bg-elevated, --hw-border-strong) and stack above legacy Quasar dialogs at z-index 7000/7001.

Term Definition Aliases to avoid Popup The shared Vue component all haywire modals are built on. Centered or position-fixed, with optional backdrop, escape-close, and backdrop-click-close. Internal — modal authors use the helper functions below. — info_modal Single icon + title + message + OK button. Non-destructive notifications, blocked actions, status reports. — confirm_modal Title + message + Confirm/Cancel. Use danger=True for destructive confirms. — pick_modal Title + single-select dropdown + Confirm/Cancel. Pre-populated to the first option. — rename_modal Title + single name input with live classification (same / changed / existing collision) + Confirm/Cancel. The confirm button relabels per state. — save_as_modal The path-prompt variant of rename_modal: directory + filename input with extension control. — diff_modal Title + sectioned diff body (DiffSection blocks) + up to two action buttons + Cancel. Reusable for any "preview changes, pick how to apply" surface; no current caller. (new) —

docs.title: Editor instance-mode terms
docs.text:
• OpenBehavior — Enum on EditorIdentity declaring how an editor's tabs come into being. Three values (members are uppercase; .value strings are lowercase):
  • REQUIRED ("required"): exactly one tab, always present, auto-populated at startup, uncloseable.
  • ON_CONTEXT ("on_context"): singleton tab, on-demand. Content mirrors a slice of session context; the tab has no binding_id. Closeable. Not persisted.
  • ON_PAYLOAD ("on_payload"): per-binding_id tab, on-demand. The binding.binding_id is both the tab's identity and its content source. N tabs allowed. Closeable. Persisted across restart.
  • on_focus — BaseEditor lifecycle hook called by Slot._activate when a binding transitions from not-active to active. Editors that own a slice of session state (e.g. GraphEditor owns active_graph) override it to mutate the context and broadcast the corresponding event. Replaces the shell-side context_field / OPEN_GRAPH_REQUESTED dispatch.
  • binding_id (tab) — A str that disambiguates per-binding_id tabs of the same editor class. For GraphEditor the binding_id is the graph path; for FileViewer it is the file path. Stored in TabState.metadata.binding_id and mirrored in EditorWrapper.binding_id. The same string is the key used in GraphAppState, the workspace-persisted identity in slot.to_snapshot, and the disambiguator in EditorWrapper.editor_binding_id.

docs.title: Signals
docs.text:
See guides/signals.md for authoring patterns; architecture/studio §2.5 for the bus dispatch model.

Term Definition Aliases to avoid Signal The base class for everything dispatched on the per-session bus. Frozen dataclass with kw_only=True; cross_session: ClassVar[bool] = False controls broadcast routing. See session/signals/signal.py Event (deprecated; was the old base class), message CommandSignal A Signal subclass for imperatives — "do X" rather than "X happened". Concrete commands include Reveal, Close, BroadcastClose LifecycleCommand (deprecated; was the old name) SignalBus Per-session typed pub/sub. One instance per Session; subscribers register a handler for an exact Signal subclass; publishes fan out by type(signal) exact match. See session/signals/bus.py EventBus (deprecated) SignalSource Abstract base class that hosts of signal_fields must inherit. Concrete implementors: SessionContext, SessionState, AppState. Declares the @abstractmethod _signal_emit(signal) contract — signal_field Descriptor declaring a reactive field on a SignalSource subclass. Writes emit a synthetic Signal subclass keyed by the field reference; reads return the stored value via bare attribute access. See session/signals/descriptor.py reactive_field (deprecated) Synthetic signal class The Signal subclass generated by signal_field at class-definition time, one per (host_class, attr_name) pair. Accessed via class-level attribute (SessionContext.active_file). Used as the subscription key — Hand-authored signal A Signal (or CommandSignal) subclass declared explicitly by a library or framework author. Carries payload fields. Emitted via session.publish(signal_instance) Custom event class (use "hand-authored signal") _signal_emit The publish method on SignalSource subclasses. SessionContext forwards to self.session.publish; SessionState derefs self.session() weakref; AppState derefs self._session_manager() and calls broadcast. Internal — never called directly by author code — cross_session ClassVar[bool] on a Signal subclass; when True, Session.publish routes via SessionManager.broadcast so every session receives the signal. Auto-set to True for synthetic signals on AppState hosts — @redraw_on(*signal_types) Editor / panel handler decorator. Subscribes the method to each signal type; after dispatch, the framework calls wrapper.redraw() exactly once per pass. Accepts both synthetic-signal class references (SessionContext.active_file) and hand-authored Signal subclasses @redraw_on(*event_types) (parameter renamed) @react_on(*signal_types) Editor / panel handler decorator for pure side-effects without redraw. Same subscription model as @redraw_on; only differs in that the framework does not call redraw() after — Reactive field (historical) The pre-unification term for what is now a signal_field. The old Reactive[T] wrapper, .value accessor, and iter_reactive_fields helper were deleted in the signal-field unification Use signal_field going forward Signal-defining library The library that declares a Signal subclass (or hosts a signal_field). Subscribers in other libraries must list it in their own LibraryIdentity.dependencies so hot-reload reloads them as a pair — otherwise isinstance checks after a reload spuriously return False — Flyout menu A nested context-menu submenu that opens on hover of its anchor item and cascades to the right (anchor="top end" self="top start"), raised above the context-menu popup (z-index 7100 > 7001). Only one open path from the root exists at a time: opening one flyout closes its siblings (same-level group) and their open descendants, via an explicit _close_flyout cascade — closing on click-away is left to Quasar's auto-close. The fragile hover-open / sibling-close mechanics are used by the add-node menu through a common flyout primitive. See [.insights/feedback_nicegui_nested_menu_flyouts.md] submenu, cascade menu, nested QMenu Setting-row menu The right-click context menu on a settings-row label cell (native ui.context_menu, scoped to the label so widget inputs keep the browser menu) — the sole promote surface. Composition rule: structural facts hide, transient facts disable — Promote-to-inlet/outlet entries appear only for eligible directions on an unpromoted, node-bound field (swapping to Demote once promoted; absent entirely on node-less bags); Reset is permanently listed for writable fields but greyed while the row is clean or its effective UiState is DISABLED (promotion stays active on DISABLED rows — chrome-locked, not value-locked, ADR 0020). A row with zero possible actions (e.g. promotable=NONE on watch()) gets no menu. Replaces the canvas Promote-Setting flyout (removed 2026-07-07) promote submenu, promotion menu, Promote-Setting menu (removed flyout), row context menu

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• A Graph contains zero or more Nodes and Edges; it is serialized as a .haywire file.
  • An Edge connects exactly one Outlet to exactly one Inlet; they must share the same FlowType or can be cast to a different type with the help of an Adapter chain.
  • A Node (class) defines Ports in init(); the NodeWrapper holds the live runtime state.
  • Each connected DATA port pair owns exactly one Pipe; the Pipe's is_lazy flag comes from the EdgeWrapper, not the port.
  • Assembly produces one Flow per EVENT node in the graph.
  • A Flow contains one global Control Flow DAG and one LocalizedDataFlow DAG per CONTROL node.
  • A Library scans folders in register_components() to populate registries (nodes, types, adapters, widgets, skins, themes).
  • A Haybale package is always a Library; not all Libraries are distributed as haybale packages.
  • An Editor occupies one Slot in the AppShell; an Editor may host many Panels filtered by Scope.
  • The AppShell is composed of: TopBar, ActivityBar, ContextBar, StatusBar, and the four Slots (ACTION, CONTEXT, EDIT, INFO).
  • Each Slot has a Bar and an area: the ACTION and CONTEXT slots have icon bars (ActivityBar, ContextBar); the EDIT and INFO slots have tab bars (MainTabBar, BottomTabBar).
  • The ActivityBar switches editors in the ACTION Slot; the ContextBar switches editors in the CONTEXT Slot; the ScopeToolbar (inside the PropertiesEditor) switches the active Scope.
  • Each slot's persisted state is a uniform slot snapshot dict (active_key, visible, size, editors) produced by Slot.to_snapshot() and keyed by SlotName value in workspace_state.json; there are no per-slot state dataclasses.
  • A Panel is always rendered inside a .hw-panel container and must use hui.* wrappers for any pattern covered by the design guide.
  • A Skin renders on the Graph Canvas and must use only --hw-node-* / --hw-canvas-* CSS tokens; it must not use hui.* panel wrappers.
  • Every structural colour reference in the app must use a CSS token (--hw-*); hardcoded hex or rgba values are a design violation.
  • A Node may declare one or more NodeSettings inner classes; each is accessible via its accessor name on the node instance.
  • A NodeSettings field may mirrors= a FrameworkSettings or LibrarySettings field; the value resolves through the SettingsRegistry via Three-tier resolution.
  • FrameworkSettings classes auto-register at registry init; LibrarySettings classes register via the BaseRegistry hot-reload path when their Library loads.
  • A Graph owns exactly one GraphSettings bag (graph.props, a GraphProperties instance); a NodeSettings field may use graph mirror / graph() to mirror a GraphSettings field, giving framework < graph < node resolution (ADR 0022).
  • A GraphEntry wraps exactly one Graph, one Editor and one Interpreter when it is executing; these are created/destroyed by start_execution() / stop_execution().
  • A GraphEntry structurally implements the GraphContainer protocol; source libraries register their containers into GraphAppState so GraphEditor can resolve binding_id → container on render.
  • A Haystack references zero or more GraphEntries by relative file path; it also records which graph is active and which graphs should auto-execute on load.
  • workspace_state.json stores the last-loaded Haystack name; on startup, HaywireApp auto-loads it if present.
  • The HaystackEditor displays a Haystack's entries and provides save/load Haystack actions and per-entry execution controls.
  • A Signal travels on the SignalBus; one SignalBus per Session.
  • A signal_field lives on a SignalSource subclass (SessionContext, SessionState, AppState); writes emit a synthetic signal class keyed by the field reference.
  • Hand-authored signals (Signal / CommandSignal subclasses) and synthetic ones from signal_field travel the same bus and use the same @redraw_on / @react_on subscription.
  • A Signal subclass with cross_session: ClassVar[bool] = True routes through SessionManager.broadcast and is received by every active Session.
  • A library that subscribes to another library's Signal must list the signal-defining library in its own LibraryIdentity.dependencies.
  • The Global marketplace holds only what the user opts into ([[markets]] and [[stalls]] subscriptions, optional inline [[haybales]]); the Project marketplace holds the project's own [[heaps]] plus the refresh [[caches]]. haywire init writes only the project marketplace. (new)
  • Refresh reads the Global marketplace, fetches every Subscription (one-level-deep), and writes the resolved candidates to the Project marketplace's [[caches]]. Conflict resolution applies blocked, then ignores, then heaps shadow, then first-come-first-served. (new)
  • The Library Browser's REQUIRED filter and the Library Overview Editor's Disable/Uninstall gating both use LibraryManager.get_installed_dependents() — the linked_libraries graph. The two surfaces always agree. (new)
  • A library's published manifest survives haywire share only if the Three manifest layers agree. The Detect step reports divergence; the Share flow's Review screen reconciles it. The Library Overview Editor is read-only for library pyproject dependencies — one authoring path, not two. linked_libraries is the exception, and not a second authoring path: the Edit dialog's Refresh button applies the same union rule the CLI and wizard apply, because a Linked registration is provably true and carries no author decision a second writer could clobber.

docs.title: Adding a node
docs.text: Dev: "I want to add a node that reads from a camera and fires a new frame event." Domain expert: "That's an EVENT node — it has an EXEC outlet but no EXEC inlet. It originates the Flow." Dev: "So the camera frames go out of a DATA outlet on the same node?" Domain expert: "Yes — the DATA outlet connects via an Edge to downstream CONTROL nodes. The Pipe on that Edge can be eager or lazy depending on whether you want immediate push or always-latest pull." Dev: "When I add this to a Library, how does it get discovered?" Domain expert: "Declare it in register_components() with scan_nodes(...), and the entry_point in pyproject.toml makes the whole Library discoverable at startup." Dev: "And if the user is in the Graph Canvas and selects the node, what shows in the CONTEXT Slot?" Domain expert: "The Properties Editor queries the PanelRegistry for all Panels whose poll() returns True for the node Scope. Each matching Panel renders inside a collapsible section. The ContextBar icon tells you which editor is active in the CONTEXT Slot (the right edge)."

docs.title: Haystack
docs.text: Dev: "I want to save the set of graphs I'm working on so I can come back to it later." Domain expert: "Save a Haystack — it's a named TOML file in haystacks/ that records which graphs are open. Use the save button in the HaystackEditor header." Dev: "What if one of my graphs is currently executing? Does the Haystack capture that?" Domain expert: "Yes — each graph entry in the Haystack has an execute flag. When you load the Haystack later, any graph marked execute = true will auto-start its Interpreter." Dev: "And unsaved graphs — do they go into the Haystack?" Domain expert: "No. A Haystack only stores paths to saved .haywire files. Unsaved GraphEntries (ones with no file path) are ephemeral — save the graph to disk first if you want it in a Haystack." Dev: "When I load a Haystack, what happens to the graphs I already have open?" Domain expert: "It's a full replace. If any current GraphEntries have unsaved changes, you'll get a confirmation dialog before they're discarded."

docs.title: Signals — subscribing and emitting
docs.text: Dev: "I want my editor to refresh when the user picks a different file. What should I subscribe to?" Domain expert: "SessionContext.active_file is a signal_field. Decorate your handler with @redraw_on(SessionContext.active_file) — the field reference IS the subscription key." Dev: "And if I want the handler to fire but NOT trigger a redraw — just a side-effect?" Domain expert: "Use @react_on(SessionContext.active_file) instead. Same subscription model; the framework just doesn't call redraw() after." Dev: "I also need to emit a coarse event when calibration finishes — carrying device ID, quality score, duration. That's not a single field changing." Domain expert: "That's a hand-authored signal. Declare class CalibrationCompleted(Signal): as a frozen dataclass with those payload fields, then ctx.session.publish(CalibrationCompleted(...)) from the calibration worker. Subscribers wire it the same way: @redraw_on(CalibrationCompleted)." Dev: "If my library defines that Signal and another library subscribes, anything special?" Domain expert: "Yes — the subscriber must list your library in its LibraryIdentity.dependencies. Otherwise hot-reload of your library can leave the subscriber holding a stale class reference, and isinstance checks return False."

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Dev: "I want my node to respect the library's default quality setting, but let users override it per-node." Domain expert: "Declare a NodeSettings inner class with a field that mirrors= the LibrarySettings field. The accessor name is whatever you call the inner class — self.output, say." Dev: "What if I just want to display a global flag, without letting the user edit it per-node?" Domain expert: "Use watch() instead of shadow() for that field. It renders as a greyed, non-interactive widget and is outlet-only-promotable. The value updates automatically when the FrameworkSettings source changes; writing to it directly is legal but only a naming convention discourages it — nothing enforces read-only-ness." Dev: "Where does the actual value come from when the node runs?" Domain expert: "Three-tier resolution, highest-priority set tier wins: the node's local instance value, then the workspace TOML set, then the global TOML set, then the descriptor default. Tiers are just set-or-unset — no 'force' strength. The SettingsRegistry owns that chain." Dev: "And the framework's own ExecutionSettings — does it need to be registered manually?"
